title: Linking Temperature to Microstates: New Thermodynamic Results for Inert and Non-Inert Gases
content: Here, we have shown that the temperature \((T)\) of an inert gas is proportional to \(w^{\frac{k_B}{nC_p}}\), where \(w\) is the number of microstates, \(n\) is the number of moles and \(C_p\) is the molar heat capacity at constant pressure and \(k_B\) is the Boltzmann constant.  The above relationship has been found to be valid using experimental data in a wide range of temperature, e.g., \([298\,\mathrm{K}\text{--}6{,}000\,\mathrm{K}]\) for all the inert gases and we have documented their respective proportionality constants.  On the other hand, for the non-inert gases, we have shown that the number of microstates is proportional to  \[ T^{nA/k_B} \times e^{\frac{nBT}{1000k_B} + \frac{nCT^2}{2\times 1000^2\times k_B} + \frac{nDT^3}{3\times 1000^3\times k_B} - \frac{nE\times 1000^2}{T^2\times k_B}}, \] where \(A, B, C, D, E\) are coefficients of the Shomate equation for molar heat capacity at constant pressure.  For three non-inert gases, namely, Hydrogen, Nitrogen and Oxygen, here we have estimated the values of the respective proportionality constants as well.
